title: C9111 — Convertible Top Latch Switch Connector
introduction:
I read this connector like a seating chart: a place in the housing does not automatically mean a wire occupies it. The shaded cavity in the drawing makes that distinction worth noticing. Match its label to the corresponding table row instead of assuming every position has an electrical assignment.

This reference identifies the convertible-top latch-switch connector. Start with the connector identity table, use the illustrated cavity labels to find the circuit rows, then consult the separate pigtail service-part entry. The function labels distinguish the signal connection from the connection marked VPWR; they do not establish switch behavior or expected readings.

This page teaches reference reading. It does not establish physical access, the viewing direction relative to the installed connector, test conditions or replacement instructions. Size codes and the Gauge convention are unexplained. Keep circuit-wire and pigtail Gauge entries in their own contexts; this page does not select replacement wire.

edits.why: I use the broad rectangular feature on the left, the projecting features on the right and the vertical cavity labels to recognize the drawing’s arrangement. The lowest cavity is shaded. These are landmarks within the illustration, not instructions for orienting or probing the installed connector. The adjacent identification row ties the drawing to its harness and shell reference.

edits.text: Match Cavities to Their Circuit Rows
edits.why: Follow each illustrated cavity label to its matching Cavity row, then read across for the circuit identifier, color, gauge, function and terminal reference. The shaded lowest position has no circuit assignment, is marked unused and has no applicable terminal part number. It is an unassigned position in this reference, not evidence of a missing wire. The populated rows identify connection roles without specifying voltage, continuity or switch-state results.

Read the service-part entry across as a single record, keeping its material, cavity count, image filename and engineering shell together. A pigtail’s housing capacity does not mean every position is assigned in this vehicle connection. The catalog entry identifies the listed service assembly; it does not provide installation, terminal-transfer or splicing instructions.
